_meta.description: Single source of truth for all game ScriptableObjects. Run MobileIdleBuilder > Import Game Data in the Unity Editor to generate or update all assets.

conventions.cross_refs: Use the string 'id' of the target object. Importer resolves to SO reference.
conventions.asset_paths: Project-relative Unity paths (Assets/...). Use 'TODO' for unknown paths — importer will log a warning and leave the field null.
conventions.arrays: Empty arrays [] mean no entries. null and [] are equivalent for the importer.
conventions.comments: Keys prefixed with '_' are ignored by the importer and are purely for documentation.

game_config._comment_purchase_scaling: Each successive placement of the same building type costs more. Formula: base_cost × multiplier^(n-1) where n = number of buildings of that type already placed.

tiers.description: Fundamental particles harvested from quantum fields. Quarks and leptons, the building blocks of everything.
Assembling nucleons and electrons into complete atoms. The domain of chemistry and the periodic table.
Combining atoms into molecules and simple compounds. Chemistry at the scale of bonds and reactions.
Refining molecules into alloys, composites, and advanced materials with engineered properties.
Fabricating high-precision components for megastructures. The frontier of material science.

research._comment: First research — unlocked from the start of the tutorial
research.description: Harness the strong nuclear force to bind quarks into protons and neutrons — and combine them with electrons to form the first atoms.
research.codex_entry: The foundational discovery enabling nucleon synthesis. By controlling the strong force, quarks can be permanently bound into stable protons and neutrons.

research.description: Combine a proton and an electron to form the simplest atom: hydrogen.
research.codex_entry: The simplest atom: one proton orbited by one electron. Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe and the gateway to all atomic chemistry.

research.description: Unlocks the Harvester — a field collector that gathers particles continuously without manual input.
research.codex_entry: Continuous field collection without manual input. A Harvester placed on a quantum field extracts particles automatically at its rated output rate.

research.description: Unlock the Atomic Assembler and the ability to build complete atoms from nucleons and electrons.
research.codex_entry: Combining protons, neutrons, and electrons into stable atoms. Each element's identity is defined by its proton count — change it and you change the element.

research.description: Unlock the Nucleon Harvester special upgrade for paired field harvesters on opposing polarity fields.
research.codex_entry: Two harvesters on opposing polarity fields can be merged into a single Nucleon Harvester, producing protons or neutrons directly without quark combination.

research._comment: Field tap-cooldown reduction branch — purely a manual-collection modifier, gates no buildings/items
research.description: Field tap cooldown is 15% shorter.
research.codex_entry: Refining the extraction pulse lets a field recharge faster after each manual tap, shortening the wait between collections.

research.description: Field tap cooldown is a further 20% shorter.
research.codex_entry: A tuned resonance cascade drives field recharge near its physical limit, collapsing the cooldown between taps.

research.description: Unlock the Isotopic Manipulator to add or remove neutrons from base elements, creating isotopes.
research.codex_entry: An element's identity is its proton count, but its neutron count determines its isotope. Isotopes of the same element have identical chemical properties but vastly different nuclear behaviour.

research.description: Unlock synthesis of uranium and other heavy elements in the Atomic Assembler.
research.codex_entry: Beyond iron, fusion in stars becomes energy-negative. Only cosmic violence — supernovae, neutron star collisions — forges the heavy elements. We replicate that violence, precisely.

research.description: Unlock uranium enrichment to U-235 and decay particle containment buildings.
research.codex_entry: Some isotopes are inherently unstable, shedding mass as alpha or beta particles. With proper containment, decay is not a hazard — it is a resource.

research.description: Unlock synthesis of beryllium and boron — the lightest solid elements beyond lithium.
research.codex_entry: The lightest solid elements: beryllium, harder than steel and lighter than aluminium; boron, an exotic metalloid with industrial and nuclear applications.

research.description: Unlock nitrogen, aluminum, and nickel — spanning organic chemistry to industrial metals.
research.codex_entry: Nitrogen dominates Earth's atmosphere and every protein chain. Aluminum is the most abundant metal in the crust. Nickel stabilises steel and powers rechargeable batteries.

research.description: Unlock copper and zinc — the workhorses of electrical engineering and metallurgy.
research.codex_entry: Copper carries electricity better than any common metal. Zinc prevents corrosion and is half of brass. Together they defined the Bronze and Brass Ages.

research.description: Unlock silver and gold — rare, noble, and indispensable in electronics.
research.codex_entry: Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of any element. Gold resists corrosion absolutely — every circuit connector in space relies on it.

research.description: Unlock platinum and tungsten — extreme performance metals for high-temperature and catalytic applications.
research.codex_entry: Platinum catalyses the reactions that make fuel cells possible. Tungsten has the highest melting point of any element — used in rocket nozzles and light filaments.

research.description: Unlock plutonium — heavier than uranium, only stable in carefully controlled nuclear conditions.
research.codex_entry: Plutonium does not occur naturally on Earth — it must be synthesised. Its fissile isotope Pu-239 is the most energy-dense fuel known to conventional physics.

research.description: Unlock the Molecular Synthesizer — combine elements into molecules and pure compounds.
research.codex_entry: Atoms combine into molecules through covalent and ionic bonds. Water, methane, and ammonia are the feedstocks of planetary chemistry — and industrial civilisation.

research.description: Unlock silica, iron oxide, and uranium hexafluoride — critical industrial and nuclear compounds.
research.codex_entry: Silica is the basis of glass and semiconductors. Iron oxide rusts and builds — it is the ore steel begins from. Uranium hexafluoride enables isotope separation by gaseous diffusion.

research.description: Unlock the Materials Forge — synthesise steel, carbon fibre, and titanium alloy from molecules.
research.codex_entry: Steel defined the industrial age. Carbon fibre enables spacecraft. Titanium alloys survive re-entry. Materials science is the discipline that turns molecules into civilisation.

research.description: Unlock semiconductor wafers, aerogel, superconductors, and metamaterials.
research.codex_entry: Semiconductor wafers are the substrate of computation. Aerogel is the lightest solid material. Superconductors carry current with zero resistance. Metamaterials bend light and gravity around themselves.

research.description: Unlock the Component Fabricator — assemble quantum processors, plasma rings, and antimatter cells.
research.codex_entry: Quantum processors harness superposition for computation. Plasma containment rings confine stellar material. Antimatter cells store energy at matter-annihilation density.

research.description: Unlock Dyson nodes, orbital frames, and graviton lenses — the components of a Dyson sphere.
research.codex_entry: A Dyson sphere captures all energy output of a star. Dyson nodes are the structural anchors. Orbital frames are the load-bearing superstructure. Graviton lenses stabilise the whole assembly against tidal forces.

research._comment: --- LOGISTICS NODES: unlock per-building capacity upgrades ---
research.description: Unlock Output Capacity upgrades on every building, so automated production keeps stockpiling instead of stalling when output buffers fill.
research.codex_entry: Once production runs unattended, the bottleneck shifts from speed to storage. Containment fields let a building hold far more finished output before it must pause — the foundation of idle stockpiling.

research.description: Unlock Input Capacity upgrades on every building, so multi-stage chains keep their intake buffers full between conveyor deliveries.
research.codex_entry: As production chains lengthen, a building can starve waiting on its conveyors. Larger feedstock buffers smooth intake so multi-input recipes run without interruption.

research.description: Unlock the 4d and post-transition metals of period 5 — rubidium through xenon.
research.codex_entry: The second row of transition metals: catalytic, refractory, and the rare-earth precursors. Bridging the periodic table from the everyday metals toward the lanthanides.

research.description: Unlock the lanthanide series and the dense period-6 metals — cesium through radon.
research.codex_entry: The rare earths power magnets, lasers, and phosphors; the heavy metals below them mark the edge of stability where the first natural radioactivity appears.

research.description: Unlock accelerator synthesis of the superheavy elements — mendelevium through oganesson.
research.codex_entry: Beyond fermium, nuclei survive only by slamming lighter atoms together at relativistic speed. Each new element exists for fractions of a second — and is worth a fortune in captured entropy.

research.description: Unlock the Fusion Reactor — fuse light nuclei into heavier ones, the shortcut up the ladder toward iron.
research.codex_entry: Stars fuse hydrogen into helium and onward, releasing binding energy at every step up to iron. The Fusion Reactor reproduces that ladder: combine two cheap light nuclei into one heavier, more valuable atom.

research.description: Unlock the alpha-capture chain — oxygen through silicon by successive helium fusion.
research.codex_entry: In evolved stars, helium nuclei (alpha particles) are captured one at a time: oxygen, neon, magnesium, silicon. Each capture climbs the fusion ladder by two protons.

research.description: Unlock the terminal fusion rungs — sulfur through iron, the natural peak.
research.codex_entry: The last day of a massive star: silicon burning forges its way to iron-56, the most tightly bound nucleus. Fusion can climb no further — beyond iron it costs more energy than it yields.

research.description: Unlock Uranium and Plutonium fields — the on-ramp for heavy matter that fusion cannot reach.
research.codex_entry: Matter heavier than iron has no cheap fusion route — it must enter the economy from a fissile field. Harvest uranium and plutonium to feed the fission ladder back down toward iron.

research.description: Unlock the Fission Reactor — split fissile nuclei into mid-weight fragments worth far more than their fuel.
research.codex_entry: A slow neutron splits a heavy fissile nucleus into two mid-weight fragments — each closer to iron, and each worth far more than the cheap fuel that produced it. The fragments and spare neutrons are caught for reuse.

items.codex_entry: One of two quark flavours that compose protons and neutrons. Carries a +2/3 electric charge. Quarks are permanently confined — they cannot exist freely outside a hadron.
The heavier of the two light quarks, carrying a -1/3 electric charge. Two down quarks and one up quark bind together to form a neutron.
A fundamental lepton with a -1 charge. Orbits the nucleus of atoms and determines all chemical bonding behaviour. No internal structure has ever been detected.
A baryon composed of two up quarks and one down quark, bound by the strong nuclear force. The number of protons in a nucleus defines which element it is — this number is the atomic number.
A baryon composed of one up quark and two down quarks. Electrically neutral. Adding or removing neutrons from a nucleus produces isotopes of the same element.
The simplest and most abundant element in the universe. One proton, one electron — the starting point for all atomic chemistry. The primary fuel of stars.
The second lightest element, produced in stellar cores through hydrogen fusion. A noble gas — chemically inert. Its nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons) is identical to an alpha particle.
A soft alkali metal and the lightest solid element. Critical in battery technology — the backbone of rechargeable batteries used in every mobile device.
The basis of all organic chemistry. Carbon's ability to form four bonds makes it the backbone of life. Also exists as graphite, diamond, and graphene.
The third most abundant element in the universe. Highly reactive and essential for combustion and respiration. Makes up 21% of Earth's atmosphere.
A semiconductor at the heart of modern electronics. Silicon wafers are the foundation of processors, solar cells, and transistors.
The most common element on Earth by mass. The endpoint of stellar fusion — stars cannot fuse elements heavier than iron without consuming more energy than they produce.
The heaviest naturally occurring element. Radioactive — decays slowly over billions of years. The primary fuel for nuclear fission reactors. Requires advanced assembly techniques.
A stable isotope of hydrogen with one added neutron. Found naturally in heavy water. An essential fuel for nuclear fusion reactions alongside tritium.
A radioactive isotope of hydrogen with two neutrons. Undergoes beta decay with a 12.3-year half-life. Combined with deuterium in the most efficient known fusion reaction.
A radioactive isotope of carbon used in archaeological dating. Its predictable decay rate allows scientists to estimate the age of organic materials up to 50,000 years old.
The fissile isotope of uranium used in nuclear reactors and weapons. Splitting U-235 releases enormous energy and produces alpha particles as decay byproducts.

Emitted during alpha decay of heavy radioactive isotopes. Equivalent to a helium-4 nucleus: 2 protons + 2 neutrons. Collected by Radioactive Containment buildings and used as a secondary energy currency.
Emitted during beta decay of unstable isotopes like Tritium and Carbon-14. A high-energy electron. Collected by Radioactive Containment buildings and fed back into the power grid.
Harder than steel and lighter than aluminium. Beryllium is transparent to X-rays and used in nuclear reactor reflectors. Toxic in dust form — handle with care.
A metalloid bridging metals and nonmetals. Boron carbide is one of the hardest materials known. Boron-10 absorbs neutrons, making it essential for nuclear reactor control rods.
78% of Earth's atmosphere. Nitrogen is the limiting nutrient in agriculture — the Haber process that synthesises ammonia from it feeds half of humanity.
The most abundant metal in Earth's crust, yet rare in pure form before electrolysis was discovered. Lightweight and corrosion-resistant — the backbone of aerospace and packaging.
A transition metal with strong magnetic properties. Critical in stainless steel, lithium-nickel battery cathodes, and superalloys that survive jet engine temperatures.
The best electrical conductor among common metals. In our Quantum Foundry, copper is synthesised atom by atom — ironic, given it is the cheapest ore in simpler mining games.
Zinc galvanises steel against corrosion and is half of brass alloy. Essential in human biology as a cofactor in hundreds of enzymes.
The highest electrical and thermal conductivity of any element. Used in solar panel contacts, antibacterial coatings, and high-performance circuit connections.
Chemically inert, immune to corrosion, and malleable beyond any other metal. Every connector in space hardware is gold-plated. Its rarity is a product of neutron star collisions.
The premier catalytic metal. Platinum in catalytic converters eliminates toxic exhaust. In fuel cells it enables hydrogen-oxygen reactions at room temperature. Rarer than gold.
The highest melting point of any element — 3,422°C. Rocket nozzles, light filaments, and plasma-facing components in fusion reactors all rely on tungsten's thermal extremity.
Does not occur naturally on Earth — only made in reactors and particle accelerators. Pu-239 is the most energy-dense fissile fuel known. Assembling it requires exquisite precision.
Hydrogen cooled to −253°C, just 20 degrees above absolute zero. The most energy-dense chemical rocket propellant by mass. Used as a feedstock for fuel cells and semiconductor processing.
Two hydrogen, one oxygen — the universal solvent and prerequisite for life as we know it. In the Foundry it is a chemical intermediate and coolant feedstock.
The simplest hydrocarbon. Natural gas is mostly methane. SpaceX's Raptor engine burns it with oxygen. A key carbon feedstock for synthesising carbon fibre and polymers.
The Haber–Bosch synthesis of ammonia is arguably the most important industrial reaction in history — it enabled fertilisers that now feed half the world's population.
Silicon dioxide — the primary component of sand, glass, and quartz. Ultrapure silica is the substrate from which semiconductor wafers are grown.
Iron oxide — rust — is the thermite reaction's fuel and the precursor ore for steel production. In the Foundry we synthesise it directly from pure iron and oxygen.
UF₆ is the gaseous compound used in uranium enrichment centrifuges. Its production here enables isotope separation and is a prerequisite for superconductor synthesis.
Iron alloyed with controlled carbon content. The structural material of the industrial age — bridges, skyscrapers, ships. Synthesised here by reducing iron oxide with methane.
Crystalline carbon arranged in long chains — five times stronger than steel at one quarter the weight. The structural material of spacecraft, racing vehicles, and megastructures.
Titanium alloyed with aluminium and vanadium — the aerospace standard. Survives re-entry temperatures, resists saltwater corrosion, and biocompatible enough for implants.
Ultrapure crystalline silicon sliced to sub-millimetre thickness. The substrate on which every integrated circuit is etched. Grown from molten silica in hydrogen atmosphere.
The lightest solid material ever synthesised — 99.8% air by volume. An extraordinary thermal insulator. Used in Mars rover heat shields and as structural fill in megastructures.
A material with zero electrical resistance below its critical temperature. Enables MRI machines, maglev trains, and the magnetic confinement coils of fusion reactors.
Engineered at the nanoscale to have properties impossible in natural materials — negative refractive index, electromagnetic cloaking, and exotic gravitational interactions.
A processor that harnesses quantum superposition and entanglement. Factorises problems in polynomial time that classical computers cannot solve in the lifetime of the universe.
A toroidal magnetic confinement structure that holds stellar plasma at 150 million degrees — hotter than the sun's core. The heart of a fusion power plant or a miniature star.
A magnetic bottle storing antihydrogen — matter's mirror. When antimatter meets matter, 100% of both masses convert to energy per E=mc². The most energy-dense storage known.
The structural anchor point of a Dyson sphere. Each node bears the gravitational tension of thousands of square kilometres of solar-collecting surface. Built to last a million years.
The load-bearing superstructure of a megastructure. Woven from titanium alloy and carbon fibre into a tensegrity lattice strong enough to encircle a star.
A metamaterial array that bends spacetime curvature. Compensates for tidal forces across the inner surface of a Dyson sphere, maintaining structural integrity against the star's gravity gradient.

recipes._comment: Uranium-235 is made by REMOVING 3 neutrons from U-238. The neutron_adjustment field here is empty because no neutrons are added — the building handles removal differently.

buildings.description: Extracts fundamental particles from quantum fields. Output depends on the field type it is placed on.
buildings._note_special_upgrade: Two adjacent harvesters on opposing polarity fields can be merged into a Nucleon Harvester.
buildings.tutorial_note: First building the player can place. Goes on the quark or lepton field. Unlocked by Automation I research.
buildings.codex_entry: Extracts fundamental particles from quantum fields. Place on a field to begin harvesting. Positive fields yield Up Quarks, negative fields yield Down Quarks, lepton fields yield Electrons.

buildings.description: Binds quarks into protons and neutrons using the strong nuclear force. Requires a power source within link range.
buildings.obsolete_condition: Nucleon Harvester unlocked — the Strong Force Combiner is no longer needed.
buildings.tutorial_note: First powered building. Placement triggers the power system tutorial segment.
buildings.codex_entry: Uses the strong nuclear force to bind quarks into nucleons. Requires a power source within range to operate. Becomes obsolete once the Nucleon Harvester upgrade is unlocked.

buildings.description: Generates electron volts (eV) to power nearby buildings. Link multiple generators to share power across the grid.
buildings.tutorial_note: Introduced immediately after the Strong Force Combiner. Teaches power radius and the energy grid.
buildings.codex_entry: Generates electron volts (eV) to power nearby buildings. Place within link range of powered buildings. Link multiple generators to share power across the grid.

buildings._comment: --- SPECIAL BUILDINGS (available from start, no research required) ---
buildings.description: Sorts raw particles from your inventory and converts their energy into base currency. The act of sorting increases local entropy — a price the Demon gladly pays.
buildings._note_entropy: EntropySinkTag is added by BuildingPlacer/BuildingAuthoring when is_entropy_sink=true. EntropySinkSystem handles conveyor-fed deposits (BuildingInputSlot). MaxwellsDemonController handles manual drag-and-drop deposits (InventorySlot). Both paths coexist.
buildings._note_demon_input: Maxwell's Demon is a pure entropy sink — no production output buffer. base_max_input_items_per_slot is 0 because it accepts all incoming items without limit (unlimited deposit queue).
buildings._note_demon_upgrades: output_rate here means throughput multiplier — how many items/second the Demon can process from conveyors. L2=2x, L3=4x base throughput.
buildings._note_demon_storage: Storage upgrades increase the Demon's internal pending-deposit queue size (items waiting to be processed for entropy).
buildings.tutorial_note: Pre-placed on the starting grid. Player deposits manually-collected particles here to earn the 100 base currency needed for Recombination I.
buildings.codex_entry: A thermodynamic thought experiment made real. Maxwell's Demon appears to violate the second law by sorting particles — but information erasure always costs energy. That cost manifests as entropy. The currency it generates is real. So is the entropy.

buildings.description: Assembles nucleons and electrons into atoms. Starts with hydrogen; research Atomic Assembly to unlock heavier elements. Power cost scales with atomic mass.
buildings._note_power: v1 power-draw: static per-level eV draw (recipe-dynamic draw deferred). Legacy intent: atomic_mass × game_config.atomic_assembler_ev_per_mass_unit
buildings._note_ports: Output exits the South (front) edge. Input.Facing = item travel direction, so the intake is on the OPPOSITE edge: West-facing -> East edge, East-facing -> West edge, South-facing -> North edge. Gives intakes on the E/W/N edges and the output on the S edge.
buildings.codex_entry: Combines protons, neutrons, and electrons into complete atoms. Power cost scales with the complexity of the element being assembled — heavier elements demand more energy.

buildings.description: Adds or removes neutrons from a base element to produce isotopes. Slower than the Atomic Assembler by design.
buildings._note_power: v1 power-draw: static per-level eV draw (recipe-dynamic draw deferred). Legacy intent: neutrons_adjusted × game_config.isotopic_manipulator_ev_per_neutron
buildings.codex_entry: Adds or removes neutrons from a base element to produce isotopes. Radioactive isotopes produced here will emit decay particles over time if housed in a Radioactive Containment building.

buildings.description: Required housing for any building producing radioactive isotopes. Safely contains decay events and harvests alpha and beta particles.
buildings._note_footprint: Houses the Isotopic Manipulator inside it — larger footprint.
buildings._note_containment: The Containment building collects decay particles from the Manipulator inside it. base_max_output_items is the particle collection buffer.
buildings.codex_entry: Required housing for any building producing radioactive isotopes. Safely contains decay events and harvests alpha and beta particles as usable energy currency.

buildings.description: Combines elements into molecules and simple compounds. The first step beyond atomic assembly.
buildings._note_power: v1 power-draw: static per-level eV draw (per-recipe draw deferred).
buildings.codex_entry: Drives covalent bond formation between elements at high energy density. Primary intake accepts the dominant element; secondary intake accepts the reactant. Output is one molecule unit per cycle.

buildings.description: Synthesises alloys and advanced materials from molecular precursors.
buildings._note_power: v1 power-draw: static per-level eV draw (per-recipe draw deferred).
buildings.codex_entry: Operates at extreme temperatures and pressures to force molecular precursors into stable alloy lattices. Slower than the Molecular Synthesizer by design — materials science demands patience.

buildings.description: Assembles advanced materials into high-precision megastructure components.
buildings._note_power: v1 power-draw: static per-level eV draw (per-recipe draw deferred).
buildings.codex_entry: The pinnacle of in-Foundry manufacturing. Operates at near-quantum precision, assembling materials into components that will eventually orbit a star. Each cycle takes minutes. Each output lasts millennia.

buildings.description: Fuses two light nuclei into a heavier element — the fast lane up the fusion ladder. Unlocked by Stellar Fusion research.
buildings._note_power: Static per-level eV draw. Nuclear reactors are high-draw consumers.
buildings._note_ports: Inputs on E/W/N edges, output on the S edge (mirrors the Atom Generator).
buildings.codex_entry: A magnetic-confinement chamber that forces light nuclei together against their mutual repulsion. Far faster than assembling heavy atoms nucleon-by-nucleon, but it only climbs as high as iron.

buildings.description: Splits a fissile nucleus with a neutron into mid-weight fragments. Unlocked by Nuclear Fission research.
buildings._note_power: Static per-level eV draw. Nuclear reactors are high-draw consumers.
buildings._note_ports: Inputs on E/W/N edges, output on the S edge (mirrors the Atom Generator).
buildings.codex_entry: A shielded rod-array core. A slow neutron splits a heavy fissile nucleus into two fragments closer to iron, releasing more neutrons to sustain the chain.

fields.codex_entry: A region of space dense with confined quarks. Positive-polarity zones yield Up Quarks; negative-polarity zones yield Down Quarks. Tap to extract a particle, then wait out the field's recharge.
A region saturated with free leptons. Tap to collect an Electron, then wait out the field's recharge. Electrons are essential for completing any atom.
A seam of naturally fissile ore. Tap or harvest to extract uranium — the cheapest on-ramp to matter heavier than iron, and the fuel for fission.
A bred-actinide deposit. Harvest plutonium — denser fission fuel, and the gateway to the transuranic ladder.

_sites_note: Quantum Domains — additional build sites. field_overrides reference 'fields' ids; density_multiplier scales that field's spawn density on this site (0.0 = absent). site_origin uses the default field set.

sites._note_fissile: uranium_field/plutonium_field are NOT in the default FieldGenerator list; their density_multiplier is read as an absolute field count for this site (see FieldGenerator.IntroducedFields).

_managers_note: Hireable building managers (Idle Planet Miner-style crew). Each grants ONE passive bonus to ONE assigned building. bonus_type: CraftSpeed (multiplies ProductionSpeed), OutputQuantity (multiplies recipe output, floor), PowerDiscount (reduces eV draw; bonus_value is the multiplier kept, e.g. 0.8 = -20%). hire_cost_prestige is in prestige currency. Hired managers + assignments survive prestige.

lines.text: Welcome. I am The Architect — your guide through the Quantum Foundry. This facility builds matter from scratch, starting with the smallest particles in existence.
Everything solid in the universe — planets, stars, you — began as fundamental particles. Your job is to harvest them, combine them, and build upward.
See that glowing blue field? That is a Lepton Field — saturated with free electrons. Every atom you will ever build needs them.
Tap it. Pull electrons into your inventory.
Good work. Those electrons gave you your first entropy — the currency that powers this facility. But entropy alone cannot build matter.
That orange field is a Quark Field. It generates Up Quarks and Down Quarks in equal measure every time you mine it — the raw ingredients for every proton and neutron you will ever craft.
Excellent work. You've synthesized protons and neutrons and converted them to entropy — the fundamental energy of this facility.
The field glows where particles accumulate. Tap it to pull electrons into your inventory.
Maxwell's Demon extracts entropy from the energy difference between sorted particles. Deposit what you have collected.
Drag the electrons to the deposit side. The Demon converts particle energy into entropy — the base currency of this facility.
Good. Those electrons built your first entropy. It is a small number for now.
Quarks carry more energy potential than leptons. The Demon will extract more entropy from them. Bring them in.
Deposit all of them. Notice how much more entropy quarks generate compared to electrons. Organized matter will generate more still.
You have enough to begin. Open the menu on the left — the Research panel is there.
The research tree is your progression map. Each node unlocks new processes, new materials, new machinery. Nothing in this facility advances without it.
Recombination I. This unlocks the strong nuclear force — the force that binds quarks into nucleons. Purchase it.
Recombination I is active. The strong nuclear force is now at your disposal — the most powerful fundamental force in nature, and the one that makes atomic structure possible.

A proton is two Up Quarks and one Down Quark — net charge +1, the core of every hydrogen atom. A neutron is one Up Quark and two Down Quarks — net charge zero, the stabilizing mass inside every nucleus beyond hydrogen.
The recipe panel holds every synthesis process you have unlocked. Open it and find the proton recipe.
Two Up Quarks, one Down Quark, bound by the strong force. The result: a proton. Charge +1. The nucleus of the simplest atom in existence. Craft two.
Now the neutron — one Up Quark, two Down Quarks. Net charge zero, but nearly identical mass to the proton. Inside a nucleus, neutrons neutralize the repulsion between protons. Craft two.
Protons and neutrons carry significantly more energy than raw quarks. The Demon values organized matter — each layer of complexity compounds your entropy yield. Bring them in.
Deposit both the protons and the neutrons. You have built the first organized matter this facility has produced.
Complexity yields more entropy. That principle will drive every decision as this facility scales.
Hydrogen synthesis is unlocked. To build a hydrogen atom you need a proton — which you now know how to build — and one electron from the Lepton Field.
Gather your materials: 4 Up Quarks and 2 Down Quarks to build two protons, plus 2 electrons to complete the atoms.
Build the protons first. Two Up Quarks, one Down Quark each. Two protons means two hydrogen atoms.
The final step: combine a proton and an electron. The electromagnetic attraction between the positive nucleus and the negative lepton creates a stable atomic orbital. Craft your hydrogen.
Hydrogen. Atomic number 1. The most abundant element in the observable universe — and you built two of them from quarks and energy alone.
Hydrogen atoms carry more bound energy than raw particles. Organized matter always yields more entropy — the Demon knows the difference. Bring it in.
You have enough entropy to unlock Automation I — your first engineering breakthrough. It enables the Harvester: a field collector that gathers particles on a continuous cycle, no tapping required.
This is the transition point. Manual harvesting was a lesson. The Harvester is how you scale.
Open the Research panel and purchase Automation I.
Automation I. Purchase it — then you can place your first Harvester.

The Harvester collects into its output buffer. A conveyor carries those particles to Maxwell's Demon automatically. Open the conveyor tool, then tap the tile beside the Harvester's output to set the start. Tap the tile in front of the Demon's input and I will route the belt for you. Tap the check to place it, then Finished when you are done.
Open the build menu and place a building on an open grid tile. It will begin production immediately.
Your factory is running. Buildings produce at their rated output continuously — no manual input required.

As production scales, entropy accumulates. But there is a ceiling on each run. When your net worth approaches the prestige threshold, you will have extracted most of this run's value — and it will be time to reset.
You have reached the ceiling. Prestige is not failure — it is the mechanism that converts one-time progress into permanent power.

The reset clears your inventory, buildings, and entropy. What you keep: prestige currency and a research memory discount on nodes you have already unlocked. Initiate it — you will return faster than you left.
The reset is complete. The facility rebuilds, but you are not starting over — you are starting ahead.
You carry prestige currency now. Unlike entropy, it does not reset between runs. Spend it on permanent upgrades that will accelerate every future run.
Open the upgrade shop. Each purchase compounds across every future run. Spend wisely.
Your electron pipeline is running. You already have Recombination I — the Strong Force Combiner is available to place. Keep accumulating entropy and we will put those quarks to work.
Place the Strong Force Combiner anywhere on the grid. It will show as unpowered until you connect a generator — we will handle that next.
The Generator produces electron volts — a local power field. Any powered building within its radius draws from it automatically. Place one near the Combiner.

No wiring needed — the Combiner is already inside the Generator's power field, so it comes online the moment a generator is in range. It draws 10 eV, well within the Generator's 50 eV output. Watch the power readout up top: if total draw ever exceeds supply, everything slows down.
The Combiner is powered but has nothing to process. Place a second Harvester on the quark field — it produces Up Quarks and Down Quarks in equal measure.
Connect the quark Harvester to the Combiner with a conveyor: tap the tile beside the Harvester's output, then the tile in front of the Combiner's input. Quarks will flow in continuously.

The Combiner can run both recipes at once. Enable Proton — 2 Up, 1 Down — and Neutron — 1 Up, 2 Down — simultaneously. With equal quark input, they balance each other naturally. No surplus accumulates.
Two output ports — one for protons, one for neutrons. Connect both to Maxwell's Demon. They sell for 3 entropy each.
Protons and neutrons selling automatically alongside electrons. Your factory has two income streams now. Every quark from every field finds a buyer.
The Atom Generator is available — you researched it when you unlocked Hydrogen Synthesis. Save up 350 entropy and place it.
Nucleons are selling. But a proton and an electron together can become something more. The Atom Generator takes one of each and produces hydrogen — your first complete atom. It is ready to place.
Place the Atom Generator on the grid. It draws 5 eV of power — well within your generator's current output. No new infrastructure needed.
Re-route the proton output from the Demon to the Atom Generator's proton input. Do the same for the electron Harvester output. Neutrons continue to sell — they are not needed for hydrogen.

Connect the Atom Generator's output to Maxwell's Demon. Hydrogen sells for 5 entropy. A raw proton and electron would have sold for 4 — assembly adds one entropy per cycle, and that margin compounds as you scale.
Hydrogen. One proton, one electron — the simplest atom in existence, and the most abundant in the universe. Your factory is making it continuously, without your input.
Every element above hydrogen is built the same way — more protons, more neutrons, more complexity. When you have enough entropy, research Atomic Assembly. The periodic table opens from there.
Before you start saving — your factory is running at base efficiency. Every building here can be upgraded on two separate tracks: Speed and Storage.
Speed upgrades multiply throughput. Level 2 doubles your production rate. Level 4 brings you to eight times the base. Same inputs, same power draw — delivered faster.
Storage upgrades expand the output buffer — how many items a building holds before it stalls. A larger buffer means the factory keeps running longer while you are away.
Tap the Atom Generator. We are upgrading its speed first — it is the bottleneck of your hydrogen line.
Materials Science opens a new frontier. Until now you have built within a single Quantum Domain — but the foundry can anchor to others.

Each Domain is its own build site, with a separate grid and field distribution. The Quark Sea teems with quark fields; the Lepton Storm runs thick with electrons. Anchoring to one costs entropy, but the unlock never expires — not even through prestige.
Open the menu and tap Domains to survey what is within reach. An inactive Domain keeps producing while you work elsewhere — collected the next time you return to it.
Two times throughput. The Atom Generator now produces hydrogen at twice the rate for the same input cost. Your entropy income just doubled.
The Storage track works the same way — tap the building again and you will see it below the Speed upgrade. A larger output buffer means the line keeps running while you are offline.
Both tracks reset on prestige. The entropy you invest here comes back as a discount on your next run — every upgrade makes the next cycle faster.
Your factory runs on its own. Hydrogen flows from quark to atom to entropy — that is the foundation. Everything that follows builds on this loop.
The Research panel shows your next frontier. Atomic Assembly opens the rest of the periodic table — but it costs five hundred entropy. Let the factory accumulate it.

Atomic Assembly. Every element above hydrogen follows the same principle: proton count defines the element, neutron count defines its isotope. The Atom Generator supports all of them once this is purchased.
Atomic Assembly is active. Helium-4 is now craftable — two protons, two neutrons, two electrons. It sells for twenty entropy: four times hydrogen, for roughly four times the inputs.
Lithium, Carbon, Oxygen, Silicon, and Iron are also available in the recipe panel. Each one is more complex and more valuable. Start with Helium-4 and scale up from there.
Helium-4. The second element. Formed in the first three minutes after the Big Bang through primordial nucleosynthesis — you have just replicated one of the universe's oldest reactions.
Notice the sell value: twenty entropy per atom. The complexity premium scales with atomic mass. Heavier elements cost more to build, but they are proportionally more valuable to sell.
Heavy Elements research unlocks Uranium — 92 protons, 146 neutrons, 92 electrons. Atomic mass 238. Craft time: nearly four minutes. Power cost: 1,190 electron volts. Sell value: 1,000 entropy.
Your current generators likely cannot sustain 1,190 eV. A fully upgraded Basic Generator outputs 400 eV. You will need multiple before attempting Uranium synthesis.
Heavy Elements research acquired. Uranium synthesis is now available in the Atom Generator. Check your power grid before you begin — the draw is 1,190 eV per cycle.

Uranium. 1,000 entropy for a single atom. This is the endpoint of stellar fusion — stars cannot forge anything heavier than iron without consuming more energy than they produce. What you just built required conditions found only in supernovae.
It is also radioactive. Its isotopes — particularly Uranium-235 — are where things become truly interesting. That requires Isotope Engineering.

An element's identity is its proton count. Its isotope is its neutron count. Change the neutrons and you change the nuclear behavior — mass, stability, decay mode — without changing the element itself.

The Isotopic Manipulator adds or removes neutrons from a base element. It runs at half the speed of the Atom Generator — neutron adjustment is precise work. Deuterium, Tritium, and Carbon-14 all unlock here.
Isotope Engineering is active. The Isotopic Manipulator is now available to place. It needs a power connection and inputs from your existing nucleon and element pipelines.

Route neutrons from your Strong Force Combiner to the Manipulator's neutron input. For Deuterium and Tritium, route Hydrogen to the element input. For Carbon-14, route Carbon. Each isotope uses a different base element.
Deuterium. Chemically identical to Hydrogen — but with an extra neutron in the nucleus. Stable isotopes like Deuterium can be stored indefinitely. Radioactive ones will not hold still.

Radioactive isotopes emit particles as they decay — Alpha or Beta depending on the isotope. With the right containment, those particles feed back into your power grid. The next research branch handles this.

Uranium-235 is the fissile isotope. Enrichment removes three neutrons from Uranium-238, shifting it from nearly stable to critically unstable. The process releases an alpha particle — a helium-4 nucleus ejected from the atom.

Before producing radioactive isotopes, you need a Radioactive Containment structure. It houses the Manipulator, absorbs decay events, and converts emitted particles into usable energy. Place it first.

Radioactive Isotopes research complete. The Radioactive Containment building is now available. Place it before operating the Manipulator for fissile materials — without it, decay products are uncontrolled.

The Containment structure occupies a 2×2 footprint and draws 30 eV. Place an Isotopic Manipulator inside it to handle radioactive synthesis. Alpha and Beta particles from decay are collected automatically and returned to your power grid.

Uranium-235. Enriched nuclear fuel — 3,000 entropy per atom. The alpha particle released during enrichment is recovered by your Containment building automatically: 20 eV returned to the grid per particle.
At scale, the decay particles emitted by your radioactive pipeline contribute meaningfully to your power budget. Alpha carries 20 eV. Beta carries 10. Let the decay work for you.

Alpha and Beta particles — secondary energy currency, harvested from nuclear instability. What is a hazard in any other context is a resource here. Your Containment building converts decay into power.

You have built matter from nothing — quarks to nucleons, nucleons to atoms, atoms to isotopes, isotopes to fissile fuel. This is the current frontier of the Quantum Foundry. The next tier of synthesis is ahead. Keep building.

_comment_daily_rewards: 28-day login reward calendar (UTC). Index by loginStreakIndex (0-based); loops after day 28. crystals = paid currency, entropy = base currency, prestige_currency = ascension shards.
_comment_daily_challenges: Rotating daily challenge pool. 3 drawn deterministically per UTC day (DayOfYear % poolCount). trigger matches an AchievementTrigger enum value. Progress accumulates the same way achievements do; each grants crystals on completion.
